newsitem.title: UK: Report predicts older, sicker Britons in future.
newsitem.headline: Report predicts older, sicker Britons in future.

text.p: Britain has become a nation with an ageing population, more working women, fewer babies and more divorced couples, and the current trends will continue into the next century, the government predicted in a report on Thursday.

Social Trends, an annual survey that paints a picture of the changing face of British society, said the 58.6 million population will grow until the year 2034, when it will reach 61 million, and then begin to decline.

People will live longer, but their declining years will be marred by ill health. More people will be living alone and easily cared for cats will become the preferred pet, making Britain's overriding passion for dogs a thing of the past.

"Life expectancy is increasing two years every decade," Tim Harris, who helped produce the report, told Reuters. "But because people have a higher expectation of health, people are living longer but the quality of life isn't that good."
Britain has the highest divorce rate in the European Union, while predominately Catholic Italy has the lowest, and more people who work on Sundays than anywhere else in the community.

Amost a quarter of employees in Britain, which has no minimum wage, earned less than four pounds ($6.50) an hour last year, and the country placed ninth on a scale of EU members in GDP (gross domestic product), just below the group's average but far behind Luxembourg which had the highest.
The gap between the rich, who got richer in the 1980s, and the poor who didn't, has remained the same in the early 1990s.
"We're taking more holidays than we used to and more of the holidays are abroad, and more people are taking two holidays a year," he said. "People's incomes are also rising in real terms."
Accidental deaths have fallen sharply and the death rate from heart disease fell by almost half in the last 25 years, reflecting a healthier lifestyle and fewer people who smoke.
Britain's normally grey, dismal weather also seems to have improved, following a global trend which showed that nine out of ten of the hottest days on record occurred since 1983.
But some things in tradition-bound Britain just don't change. "The pub is still the favourite place for free-time activity," said Harris. ($1=.6175 Pound)
